title: A crate-suite run leaves no schema in the test database: every case drops what it made on the test server, the cases that make several schemas included
prompt:
Read crates/spawn-postgres/tests/common/mod.rs (`schema_name`, `store`, `Schema` and its Drop, `schema_url`), crates/spawn-postgres/tests/roles.rs (`many_migrations_at_once_on_one_cluster_all_succeed`, `Database`), and every other test that makes a schema or a database on the test server (spawn-cli's `spawn_test_*` schemas among them).

The problem. The database tests run against SPAWN_TEST_DATABASE_URL, each case in a schema of its own (`spawn_test_<pid>_<nanos>_<case>`). The `Schema` guard drops the schema when the case ends. Not every case takes the guard. roles.rs's many_migrations_at_once_on_one_cluster_all_succeed makes eight schemas (`..._burst_0` to `_7`) through `schema_url` alone, and nothing drops them. Measured on 351fb1e6 (2026-11-11, each crate's tests alone against a fresh database of their own, all passing): spawn-postgres leaves 8 schemas; spawn-cli, spawn-core, spawn-host, spawn-kdf and spawn-jev leave none. On the fleet's test database (spawn_fleet_test), 2533 such schemas had piled up by 2026-11-11, 2.7 GB with their catalog rows. The lead dropped them, and the database was 128 MB after.

Required behaviour.
(a) Every case drops what it made on the test server when it ends: its schemas, the cases that make several included, anything it wrote into public, and its databases and logins as roles.rs's `Database` already does.
(b) A crate-suite run whose tests all pass leaves no schema it made in the test database, whatever its name, and nothing in the database's public schema (no table, function or type that was not there before). A schema renamed (another prefix), or tables written into public, are still left behind. This holds for every crate, not only the one the scenario runs.
(c) Nothing else changes: the same tests, the same assertions and the same number of tests. Drop only what the case made, never by a pattern over the database, since another run may share it.

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/055.sh (about 20-40 s). In the tree under test, it runs `cargo test -p spawn-postgres` once (the build is the gate's), with SPAWN_TEST_DATABASE_URL a fresh empty database of its own on the same server. Then:
- (1) the tests pass (a failing suite cannot be judged for what it leaves; the check of the tests reports it);
- (2) no schema is left but the server's own (public, information_schema, pg_*), whatever its name, and public holds no relation, function or type it did not hold before the run.
It fails with 1 at (2) on 064ef1e5: the 8 burst schemas.
Once this is solved, the owner folds the same check into the check of the tests (every crate, a fresh database per run) and retires 055.sh. So (b) holds for crates the scenario does not run.

For the implementer. `Schema`'s drop gives up quietly after a 5 s lock wait (a connection of the case still open). A case that drops its schema only after its connections close never meets that wait.

The product reason. Every gate, reviewer and worker runs the crate suites against a test database. Eight schemas per run became 2.7 GB on the fleet's test server in days, slowing every catalog lookup on it.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
